subject: Post-demo follow-up: data handling & support access
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Imani Okafor <security@acme-analytics.com>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 09:06:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: data handling & support access

Thanks for the time this morning — appreciate the detailed questions. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can align on the security bar for any pilot/POC:

Summary of what we heard you need:
- Data residency in US-only regions for workload and backups
- Clear policy for PII (names, email, customer IDs) with configurable retention windows
- Immutable audit logs for access events retained for a minimum of 2 years
- RBAC integrated with your IdP (SCIM + SAML) and least-privilege roles for support
- Break-glass flow for emergency support access with full audit trail and alerting

Questions / clarifications we need from you to scope work:
1) For PII categories: can you list the specific fields you classify as regulated PII vs. non-sensitive identifiers?
2) Are backups required to be stored in a separate account/tenant (we can set up customer-owned buckets)?
3) For break-glass, do you require an approval chain (e.g., two approvers) or is just a logged emergency justification sufficient?

Attachments: I attached a condensed security matrix that maps our controls to your asks (redwood-data-security-matrix.xlsx).

Next steps we propose:
- Technical deep-dive (30–45m) with your infra/security engineer + our infra lead (Lauren) to align on SCIM/SAML flows and retention config
- Draft a mutually agreeable support-privilege playbook (we can start from the attached template)
- Provide a scoped quote and pilot plan once we confirm residency and retention windows

If that sounds right, can you confirm availability for a deep-dive next week (Jul 20–22)?

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

--

From: Imani Okafor <security@acme-analytics.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 10:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: data handling & support access

Thanks Rishi — good summary. A few specifics from our side to help scope: 

PII classifications (we use these labels internally):
- Regulated PII: full name, personal email, national ID, date of birth, payment instrument last-4 (we tokenize but consider controlled)
- Sensitive product identifiers: customer_id, internal_user_id (these are low-risk but still must be logged)

Retention & residency:
- Audit logs and access events: minimum retention 24 months (longer if feasible)
- Short-term request payloads (model inputs): retained for 30 days by default, extendable to 365 days for troubleshooting if needed
- Backups and snapshots: must be US-only and, if possible, in a separate customer-owned bucket we can point to

RBAC / SSO:
- We require SCIM user provisioning with group sync and SAML SSO for role enforcement.
- Roles should map at least to: admin, developer, read-only-analytics, support-limited. Support role must not have direct access to raw request payloads by default.

Break-glass / support access:
- Break-glass must be time-limited (max 4 hours) and require an incident justification logged to our ticketing system.
- All break-glass events must generate an immediate email alert to security@acme-analytics.com and create an append-only audit record with requester identity, approver(s), TTL, and artifacts accessed.

Evidence / timeline:
- We need SOC2 Type II evidence and a summary of encryption-at-rest and TLS config within two weeks to support procurement.

We can do the deep-dive on Wed Jul 21 after 10am PT or Thu Jul 22 in the morning. FYI our procurement/legal team will be copied once we have the technical answers.

-Imani
Director, Security Engineering
Acme Analytics
security@acme-analytics.com

--
Please see inline comments in the matrix: row "support-access".

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Imani Okafor <security@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 08:52:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: data handling & support access

Imani — thanks for the clear breakdown. Below are how we currently map to your asks and the configurable options; I'll include Lauren on the deep-dive to cover infra specifics.

Residency & backups:
- Redwood hosted can pin workloads to US-East (customer-specific tenancy). Backups/snapshots can be exported to a customer-owned S3 bucket (we support cross-account uploads).

Retention and PII:
- Default request payload retention: 30 days (configurable). We offer policy-based labels so you can set 30/90/365 day retention per dataset.
- For regulated PII, we support field-level redaction and tokenization prior to persistent storage. We can provide a short workflow to implement client-side tokenization if you prefer no raw PII reaching our storage layer.

Logging & audit trails:
- We maintain append-only access logs (who, when, what resource, action) with integrity checks; configurable retention up to multiple years. Exports to your SIEM or a customer S3 bucket are supported.

RBAC & IdP integration:
- SCIM + SAML: supported. We map groups to roles; recommended role set: admin, dev, analyst, support-limited. Support-limited role is scoped to metadata/query interfaces and does not surface raw payloads unless break-glass is used.

Break-glass flow (our default template):
- Support requests for break-glass initiated via our support portal produce a one-time token bound to a specific session and TTL (default 4 hours).
- Approval options: (A) Logged justification + single approver (fast path) or (B) two approver flow (strict). Both flows produce an immutable audit record and send immediate email/SMS alerts to your security ops.
- All break-glass activity is exported as part of the audit bundle for post-incident review.

Evidence & compliance:
- We can provide SOC2 Type II summary and sample reports; full attestations are uploaded to our evidence portal. Encryption: AES-256 at rest, TLS1.2+ in transit.

Attachments: I've attached our support privilege playbook and a scoping checklist to speed the deep-dive (redwood-support-privilege-playbook.pdf; scoping-checklist.docx).

Next steps:
1) Schedule technical deep-dive: Lauren to run through SCIM/SAML and retention config (Lauren, are you available Wed Jul 21 10:30am PT?).
2) We'll prepare a draft playbook with the two-approver break-glass template and a scoped pilot plan for 30-day retention with option to extend.
3) Share SOC2 summary and encryption details to Imani + procurement by EOD Tue Jul 20.

If this aligns, we'll lock the time and share an agenda.

Best,
Rishi

> Thanks — one quick follow: for the break-glass token is the requester identity recorded from the IdP or can an internal Redwood operator initiate? We want requester identity to be strictly tied to SCIM-provided users.

Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: data handling & support access

Imani — quick note from the infra side:

- Break-glass requester identity: we bind break-glass tokens to the authenticated IdP identity. Internal Redwood operators cannot generate a token that obscures requester identity; any operator-initiated emergency access is recorded and tied to their SAML identity.
- We can enable SCIM group sync and provide a SCIM mapping doc during the deep-dive.
- For the deep-dive: Wed Jul 21 at 10:30am PT works for me. I will share a short agenda and the SCIM/SAML checklist before the meeting.

Marissa — I'll rely on you to coordinate procurement loop-in after the tech call.

Lauren Bishop
Engineering Lead, Infrastructure | Redwood Inference
